cells.tense: Right now you are carrying what is yours to carry, and you decide how it gets set down.
cells.ask: Say one honest thing you have been sitting on, out loud, and let it stand without adding anything to soften it.
cells.core:
You are under a real weight and you are not being bent by it. Someone who owes you something hears about it; something that can wait gets to wait. You are not keeping score and you are not pretending there is no score. That kind of weighing is running now, quietly, in how you decide what to take on and what to leave alone.

It stays only while you keep your hand on it. Grip a little harder and fairness turns into arithmetic; let it slip and the weight lands on whoever is nearest. So watch for the moment when giving stops feeling like an exchange and starts feeling like a debt. You get to make one fair offer today — say the true thing, once — and then leave the answer to them, without managing it.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying what is yours, without hardening around it.
cells.verb: Bearing weight without breaking, and without hardening around it
cells.place: In the room where what's owed and what's given get weighed

cells.tense: You are bracing for a load that has not arrived and may never be yours to take.
cells.ask: Before you answer the next request, take one full breath, then name the true amount you can take on and stop there.
cells.core:
You are holding more than this moment is asking for. The shoulders are already set for the next thing and the one after it, loads nobody has handed you. From outside it reads as strength; from where you are standing it is grip that has stopped checking whether it is still needed.

Fairness has left the room. You are carrying for people who have not asked, covering for things that have not gone wrong, and the weighing has become a permanent state instead of a response to an actual thing. The way back is not to drop any of it. It is to weigh again: say the true amount out loud once, and let that be the whole answer.

cells.tense: You are carrying less than you could, and the weight you do pick up feels heavier than it is.
cells.ask: Finish one small thing and then say out loud that it is done, to yourself or to someone, without taking on the next one yet.
cells.core:
When the pressure comes, the move now is to step out from under it rather than hold it, and stepping out has become the pattern instead of the exception. Nothing here is a failure of strength; it is a failure of trust in the strength, and the two look the same from inside.

What you cannot do from there is weigh anything. Out of the room with the weight, every request looks like too much, so you decline by default and call it sensible. The way back is not to force effort into a place that feels empty. Start where there is energy: release one thing you have already finished with. One small letting-go shows the body that release is not defeat, and bearing comes back on its own.
cells.sheetLine: The strength has not gone, it has just stopped feeling safe to use.
cells.verb: Bearing weight without breaking, and without hardening around it

cells.tense: You are doing the carrying right now and calling it nobody's job in particular.
cells.ask: Write one sentence naming something you carried this week and call it yours, then keep it where you will see it again.
cells.core:
There is strength running here that you are not claiming. People experience it — the room settles when you walk in, the weight gets spread differently because you are there — and your own account of it is that you were just doing what needed doing. It is real and it is being used. What is missing is the plain acknowledgment that it belongs to you.

What you don't own, you can't pace. You give from habit rather than choice, and there is no floor under it, so when it runs out it surprises you. The correction is not a bigger claim but a smaller one: name one specific thing you held this week, in one sentence, and call it yours. That is the whole act. What you are running on is developed enough to be seen.
cells.sheetLine: The strength you are running on is yours, even while you call it nothing.
cells.verb: Bearing weight without breaking, and without hardening around it
cells.place: In the room where what's owed and what's given get weighed

attempts.check: Unsupported claim risk: the record gives only the card, seat, status and medicine; any detail about a specific room, the who, how long, or what was learned in Too Little is not supported — it stays out. A reader could reasonably say the balance is simply discipline or habit rather than a lived calibration, so the core describes the mechanism in a moment they could recognise and never asserts their history or motive. The asks do not require a safe person, money, energy or time to be true, and each is useful even if the read is wrong: the Balanced ask is an optional offering, the Too Much ask is a physical pause before reply, the Too Little ask is a small out-loud claim, the Unacknowledged ask is one written sentence. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be anything like 'you always hold everything for everyone' — a universal about their life; it is cut, and the cells say only what the capacity is doing now.
